A little look
behind the game.

Characters, artwork, and a world taking shape.
A collection from the making of Trash Dash.

6 items

Story concept

An opening-story concept exploring why Trashy and Jimothy set out to protect their home. Created to establish the adventure’s emotional starting point, it connects the warmth of the forest with the first signs of pollution and the darker shapes of its threats.

Character design

A visual development sheet bringing the chapter-one cast into one shared world. Created to explore silhouettes, expressions, and movement, it sets out the contrast between Trashy’s compact, energetic shape and Jimothy’s taller frame, alongside a playful but threatening enemy cast.

Environment concepts

A chapter-one journey from sunlit forest paths to a polluted clearing. Created to explore how each area could feel distinct, these scenes guide the use of color, lighting, platforms, and set dressing as the welcoming woodland gives way to more dangerous ground.

Props & items

A concept catalogue of collectibles, containers, traversal objects, and forest details. Created to give small objects clear roles, it explores recognizable shapes and materials that help distinguish a reward, an obstacle, or a piece of scenery while making the world feel lived in.

Story beat storyboard

A six-beat storyboard connecting the opening forest adventure to the city beyond. Created to bring story and exploration into the same sequence, it maps the visual progression from bright, inviting woods through purple corruption to a distant skyline that promises a larger world.
